standard_prerequisites.name: The splitting principle: a morphism over which the module acquires a filtration by invertible modules, with injective pullback on Chern classes
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, label lemma-splitting-principle, invoked at proof line 8532
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the morphism to which one may pull back, since the pullback on the relevant groups is injective after any base change, which is what allows the relation to be checked after a filtration exists.

standard_prerequisites.name: The total Chern class of a module filtered by invertible modules as the product of the linear factors, and additivity in the invertible sheaf
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, labels lemma-chern-filter-by-linebundles (proof line 8555) and lemma-c1-cap-additive (proof line 8554)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first writes the total Chern classes of the module and of its dual as products of linear factors in the first Chern classes of the successive quotients and of their inverses, and the second gives that the first Chern class of an inverse is the negative of the first Chern class.

core_obligations: Reduce to the filtered case: choose the morphism supplied by the splitting principle and use that its pullback is injective after any base change, so that the identity may be proved after pulling back; hence one may assume that the module has a filtration whose successive quotients are invertible modules (proof lines 8530-8544).

Write the dual filtration: the annihilators of the pieces of the filtration form a decreasing filtration of the dual whose successive quotients are the inverses of the original invertible quotients, and the first Chern class of an inverse is minus the first Chern class (proof lines 8545-8554).

Conclude: the total Chern classes of the module and of its dual are the products of the factors one plus, respectively one minus, the first Chern classes of the invertible quotients, and the asserted sign relation follows by expanding those products; the author states that this formal computation is omitted (proof lines 8555-8563).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a module filtered by invertible quotients via the splitting principle (proof lines 8530-8544).
Construct the dual filtration with inverse quotients and take first Chern classes (proof lines 8545-8554).
Compare the two products of linear factors (proof lines 8555-8563).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the Chern classes of the dual of a finite locally free module as the alternating multiples of the Chern classes of the module itself (statement lines 8519-8528, tag 0FA5). The proof reduces to the case where the module has a filtration by invertible modules by means of the splitting principle and injectivity of pullback, constructs the dual filtration whose successive quotients are the inverses of the original quotients, and then compares the two total Chern classes written as products of linear factors with opposite signs. The construction of the dual filtration is the substance, so the claim is H2.
